LESSON: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING – SHORT STORIES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories, part of Strand 4 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why are short stories important? 2. Why is it important to ensure safety in your environment and especially roads?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work collaboratively with peers to conduct a reader’s theatre to read short stories on the theme (causes of road crashes and mitigation measures),

2. pick out vocabulary related to the theme from the short stories,

3. work jointly to conduct a spelling bee contest to spell the vocabulary identified,

4. find the meaning of the vocabulary spelt,

5. work with peers to pick out adjectives used in the text,

6. use the vocabulary and adjectives to construct simple sentences and share with peers for review,

7. collaboratively identify the main ideas of the text, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work collaboratively with peers to conduct a reader’s theatre to read short stories on the theme (causes of road crashes and mitigation measures),
2. pick out vocabulary related to the theme from the short stories,
3. work jointly to conduct a spelling bee contest to spell the vocabulary identified,
4. find the meaning of the vocabulary spelt,
5. work with peers to pick out adjectives used in the text,
6. use the vocabulary and adjectives to construct simple sentences and share with peers for review,
7. collaboratively identify the main ideas of the text, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner is motivated to learn continuously by finding the meaning of the

vocabulary spelt.

• Self-efficacy: It is enhanced as the learner shows concerted attention to manage tasks when conducting a spelling bee

contest to spell the vocabulary identified.

Values:
• Respect: It is promoted as the learner accommodates diverse opinions when sharing constructed sentences on vocabulary

for peer review.

• Responsibility: It is enhanced as the learner engages in assigned roles and duties when working with peers to conduct a

reader’s theatre.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and Security: This is promoted as the learner interacts with stories on safety in public places.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner can relate the concept of extensive reading to literary appreciation in English and Kiswahili.
